title: P0 hostedapi stream-shim failure correlation notes
body:
Summary:

This document captures the initial investigation notes for the P0 that impacted hosted API streaming on 2029-09-14 (UTC). Customers experienced partial streaming responses (early stream termination / "chops") and a correlated increase in 5xx rates for streaming endpoints for ~37 minutes. This is an SRE-led incident with engineering collaboration.

Impact:
- Scope: ~12% of streaming sessions opened in the US-W region showed early termination or truncated deltas; non-streaming (batch text generation) endpoints largely unaffected.
- Customer visible symptoms: clients saw "connection closed" mid-stream, resulting in incomplete JSON chunks in a few cases and repeated client reconnects. Latency for some requests spiked as retries queued.
- Business impact: degraded UX for streaming customers and several support tickets tied to loss of incremental tokens. No data exfiltration or incorrect model outputs recorded.

Detection and Monitoring:
- First alert: 2029-09-14T03:12:04Z via Streaming Error Rate alert (threshold 0.8% over 5m). SRE on-call acknowledged at 03:13:12Z.
- Side signals: edge TLS session rehandshake counters increased at 03:11Z; edge resource (ephemeral buffer) saturation metrics rose shortly after.
- Pager escalation at 03:16Z as the signal continued to climb.

Initial Hypothesis:
- Streaming fragmentation suggests a downstream consumer or edge-level buffering/backpressure problem. The simultaneous bump in TLS rehandshakes hints at an interaction between our stream-shim (connection adaptation layer) and the edge TLS stack.

Timeline (high level):
- 03:11Z: Small TLS rehandshake spike observed on a subset of edge nodes servicing US-W.
- 03:12Z: Streaming error rate alert fires.
- 03:14Z: Ops started isolating edge nodes by taking a small pool out of rotation; error rate dropped briefly then rebounded.
- 03:20Z: Correlation found to recent stream-shim rollout (canary completed on 2029-09-13 22:00Z) - a packaging change altered read buffer handling under EWOULDBLOCK semantics.
- 03:24Z: Decision to rollback stream-shim to previous artifact on affected edge nodes.
- 03:31Z: Rollback completed on US-W edge cluster. Error rate begins to decline.
- 03:48Z: Streaming error rate back to baseline; post-incident monitoring remains.

Root Cause Analysis (current understanding):
- The 2029-09-13 stream-shim artifact included a micro-optimization to reduce memory copies by reusing a single read buffer across multiplexed connections. Under normal conditions this reduced GC and improved throughput.
- When coupled with an increase in TLS rehandshakes (observed at ~03:11Z), the shim's read-loop incorrectly interpreted a partial TLS renegotiation event as EOF in a small percentage of cases when socket read returned EWOULDBLOCK followed by a handshake-driven packet sequence. That led to early completion signals propagating to the streaming demultiplexer and to the client as a closed stream chunk.
- The edge TLS rehandshake spike was likely triggered by a transient certificate verification load during a behind-the-scenes cert rotation in the region (cert rotation job was noisy due to concurrent cert cache flushes from a separate rollout).
- The combined timing of shim behavior + TLS noise created a race; the shim's change removed a defensive read-sanity check that previously prevented treating transient EWOULDBLOCK + renegotiation as EOF.

Why the rollback fixed it:
- Reverting to the prior shim restored the defensive check and per-connection buffer semantics, eliminating the false EOF condition.

Contributing factors:
- Incomplete canary coverage: stream-shim canary did not sufficiently exercise the edge TLS rehandshake path (canary traffic avoided cert rotation hosts).
- Lack of an explicit metric to surface "shim-treated-eof" events — we only had generic stream error counts.
- Cert rotation job produced more concurrent cache flushes than expected during a separate rollout window.

Mitigations (immediate during incident):
- Rollback stream-shim artifact on affected edges (completed by 03:31Z).
- Temporarily increase retry budget for streaming clients to reduce immediate client-visible failures.
- Quarantine the noisy cert-rotation job for the remainder of the maintenance window to prevent recurrence.

Post-incident action items (short-term):
- Add a shim-level metric: "shim.false_eof_count" and high-cardinality labels (edge-node, shim-version) — owner: Marcus Lee, due: 2029-09-20.
- Patch stream-shim to reintroduce the read-sanity check and add unit tests that simulate EWOULDBLOCK + TLS renegotiation sequences — owner: Elena Novak, PR: linked, due: 2029-09-18.
- Expand canary traffic to include nodes under cert rotation and force a canary run during a simulated rotation — owner: Ravi Sundaram, due: 2029-09-22.
- Add an SLO-bound alert for "stream-chop-rate" with a playbook link and quick rollback runbook — owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2029-09-19.

Longer-term recommendations:
- Harden stream demultiplexer to tolerate mid-handshake socket semantics and avoid treating transient read conditions as terminal.
- Improve maintenance coordination: ensure cert rotation jobs announce a low-noise window and avoid concurrent noisy rollouts in the same region.
- Introduce synthetic "renegotiate" canaries that exercise the full handshake path end-to-end in production-like conditions.
- Add a small, non-zero hold period after EWOULDBLOCK events before emitting EOF in the shim; tune against latency budgets.

Runbook updates (draft edits):
- New section: "Streaming partial-chop / false EOF"
  - Symptoms: elevated stream-chop-rate, truncated JSON / early Connection-close, correlated EWOULDBLOCK spikes or TLS rehandshake anomalies.
  - Immediate steps: 1) Check shim.false_eof_count; 2) Verify shim-version(s) rolled out in region; 3) If new shim version present, rollback to last stable; 4) Isolate affected edge nodes from LB; 5) If rollback unavailable, increase per-connection timeouts and redirect canary traffic.
  - Escalation: page runtime team + stream-shim owners immediately.

Communication notes:
- Customer comms: Draft message for support & status page prepared; emphasized that data integrity unaffected and recommended client-side reconnect/backoff settings while we rolled back.
- Internal comms: Slack incident channel created (#inc-p0-hostedapi-stream-2029-09-14). Regular updates posted every 6–8 minutes until closure.

SLA / Post-incident metrics:
- Total incident window (time > alert threshold): ~37 minutes.
- % customers affected: 12% of streaming sessions in region; estimated <0.5% of total platform token volume.
- No SLA credit determination required yet pending customer escalation review (CS lead to advise).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did the cert rotation job create a larger-than-expected rehandshake spike? Logging doesn't show a direct bug but reveals concurrently scheduled maintenance from a different services team. Owner: Ops Infra, due: 2029-09-21.
- Are there other shims or third-party libs with similar micro-optimizations that removed defensive checks? Audit recommended. Owner: Security/Runtime, due: 2029-09-30.

Postmortem conclusion (draft):
The incident was a P0 caused by a narrow race between a recent micro-optimization in the stream-shim and an unrelated cert rotation activity that increased TLS renegotiations. The optimization removed a defensive read check, allowing transient EWOULDBLOCK + handshake sequences to be interpreted as EOF. The fix was a rollback of the shim artifact, a patch to reintroduce the check, and runbook updates to detect and mitigate similar issues faster.

Owners and tracked action items (summary):
- Marcus Lee: metric shim.false_eof_count and dashboard, due 2029-09-20.
- Elena Novak: shim patch + tests, PR link in linked_artifacts, due 2029-09-18.
- Ravi Sundaram: expanded canary plan + canary run under cert rotation, due 2029-09-22.
- Aisha Patel (author): runbook edits + alerting changes, due 2029-09-19.
- Ops Infra: cert-rotation noisy run investigation, due 2029-09-21.

Appendix (investigation notes):
- Packet captures from 03:09–03:17Z show sequences where the client-facing connection returned 0 bytes read followed by TLS handshake packets; shim treated first 0 read as terminal in ~2% of those captures.
- Canary config review: the canary traffic generator used a deterministic path that avoided hosts actively undergoing cert cache flushes; adjust to probabilistic distribution in future.

Next steps: finalize patch PR, merge metric and alert changes, schedule retro with runtime and infra teams 2029-09-18 17:00Z, and publish finalized postmortem on Confluence once all owners close action items.

Notes to self:
- Avoid the term "EOF" in external comms; use "early stream termination" for clarity.
- Keep incident channel logs archived under incident SRE folder.
